268	## Claude Usage (Usage.cs / ClaudeUsageControl / ClaudeUsageToolWindow)
269	
270	- Tool window: Embeds `claude.ai/settings/usage` in a WebView2 control (`ClaudeUsageToolWindow`, GUID `C3D4E5F6-...`); opened via toolbar or menu
271	- X-button behavior: Intercepted via `IVsWindowFrameNotify2.OnClose` — calls `frame.Hide()` and returns `E_ABORT` so the WebView2 scraper keeps running in the background
272	- `ForceClose()`: Toolbar toggle calls this to fully destroy the window (WebView2 disposed); distinct from X-button hide
273	- Inline usage bars: Mini progress bars in the prompt panel showing session/weekly usage; populated from `UsageSnapshot`; hidden when scraping fails or user not signed in
274	- Snapshot caching: Last successful scrape serialized as JSON to `LastUsageJson` + `LastUsageTimestamp`; restored on startup so bars render immediately with stale data while fresh fetch runs
275	- Off-screen background scraper (issue #133): while the tool window is closed, the WebView2 is parented into a hidden top-level `Window` owned by the VS main window (`ClaudeUsageControl.EnsureOffscreenHost`, positioned at -32000/-32000, `ShowActivated=false`, `ShowInTaskbar=false`, 1024×768 so claude.ai renders its desktop layout) instead of into the tool window frame. Reason: hiding the frame tears down the WebView2's `HwndHost` (issue #131), so a frame-parented scraper can only be rebuilt by making the tab visible — which turned every background refresh into a show-hide cycle that popped the usage tab into view once a minute. `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen)` rebuilds whenever the live instance sits in the wrong host (HwndHost cannot be reparented); `OnWindowBecameVisible` therefore rebuilds into the frame on an explicit open, and the next background tick rebuilds off-screen after the tab is closed again — one rebuild per visibility change instead of one per refresh. Focus priming is suppressed via `SuppressFocus` (background init, off-screen hosting, or control not on screen) so the invisible window never takes keyboard focus
276	- Auto-refresh: `UsageAutoRefreshSeconds` setting (0 = manual); page reload triggered by the scraper — visible in the tool window when its tab is active, off-screen when it is closed, auto-hidden, or behind another tab. `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.VisibilityChanged` hands polling between the page timer and the background timer on every activation/deactivation; `UsageWindowOpened` is only persisted session-restore intent and must never be used as a live-visibility gate. Off/1m only (v67.0, floor lowered from 2m to 1m in v155.0): the 30s/1m/2m/Off combo (both in the tool window toolbar and the Settings *Usage* tab) collapsed to a single Auto-refresh checkbox meaning 0 (off) or 60 s. Because older releases persisted values below that into JSON, every read path floors a positive value to 60 (`ApplyAutoRefreshSeconds`, `StartUsageBackgroundRefreshTimer`, and the Settings dialog's `origAutoRefresh`) rather than migrating the field, so a legacy value is normalized wherever it enters. The background floor for the "Off" case is also 60 s (inline bars still need a slow refresh when the tab is not active).
277	  - `ClaudeCodeControl.Usage.cs`'s background heartbeat timer (`_usageBackgroundRefreshTimer`) always runs once bars are enabled — never gated on visibility at start time — and self-guards per tick against `_usageToolWindow.IsWindowVisible` (issue #111, two rounds): the *cached* tab-active flag that `ClaudeUsageToolWindow` maintains from `IVsWindowFrameNotify.OnShow`'s `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated`/`TabDeactivated`, not a live `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()` COM read. `IsVisible()` reports S_OK for any tool window frame that is merely open, including a tab sitting inactive behind a sibling tab in the same dock group — using it as the tick guard (a regression introduced and then reverted in the same round of fixes) made the background refresh believe the Usage tab was always "visible" whenever it was open anywhere, so the bars only ever updated on an explicit click into that tab.
278	- Session restore: `UsageWindowOpened` persisted; `InitializeUsageMonitoring()` auto-reopens the window and reloads data 2s after solution load
279	- Startup refresh of the inline bars (v159.0): after a VS restart the bars stayed on the cached snapshot for the whole session unless the user clicked into the Claude Usage tab. Several independent causes, all fixed together:
280	  - `ClaudeUsageToolWindow.OnToolWindowCreated` seeded its cached tab-active flag (`_isVisible`) from `IVsWindowFrame.IsVisible()`, which is S_OK for a frame that is merely open — exactly the state VS restores the tab in when a sibling tab in its dock group is the active one. Both background-scrape guards read that flag, so they saw "foreground tab" and never scraped. Seeding (and confirming, in `OnShow`) now goes through `IsFrameOnScreen()` → `IVsWindowFrame.IsOnScreen`, which is false for a tab parked behind a sibling. `FRAMESHOW_TabActivated` is still taken at face value; only `WinShown`/`WinRestored`/`WinMaximized` — which VS also raises for `ShowNoActivate` on an obscured tab — are confirmed against it.
281	  - The WebView2 WPF control only completes `EnsureCoreWebView2Async` once its host window renders, so the in-frame build triggered by restoring that never-rendered tab (`OnWindowBecameVisible` → `ReviveOnShowAsync`) never finished. Every `EnsureAliveAsync` caller awaits the same in-flight `_pendingWebViewInit`, so the off-screen scraper could not be built either — one hung build poisoned usage refresh for the session. `EnsureCoreWebView2WithTimeoutAsync` bounds the wait (30 s) and throws `TimeoutException`, which `InitializeWebViewAsync` handles by discarding the half-built instance *without* the WebView2-runtime error panel (it is not a runtime problem) so the next build starts clean.
282	  - `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync` no longer forces `EnsureAliveAsync(offscreen: true)` on an instance that is alive in the frame — that rebuild tears the WebView2 out of the tab it renders in (HwndHost cannot be reparented). A live instance scrapes fine wherever it is parented, so it is `Reload()`ed instead; the off-screen build is the fallback for "nothing alive" plus one retry when a reloaded frame-hosted instance stays silent for 10 s (its rendering host was already gone — issue #131).
283	  - `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync`'s `showWindow` branch kicks one `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync()` when `activate` is false (the startup restore), since a restored-but-unrendered tab never loads its page. The call self-guards on the tab-active flag, so it is a no-op when the tab really is showing.
284	- User-data folder (persistence): A single fixed `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\WebView2` folder holds the WebView2 profile so cookies/localStorage/IndexedDB survive a VS restart (devenv gets a new PID each launch — the old per-PID folder started every session logged-out, issue #62). `ClaudeUsageWebViewEnvironment.GetOrCreateAsync(primary, fallback)` falls back to a per-PID `WebView2_<pid>` folder only if `CreateAsync` throws because another VS process holds the lock. `CleanupStaleWebView2Folders()` reclaims dead `WebView2_*` folders (glob excludes the fixed `WebView2`). `shared_cookies.json` (`Load/SaveSharedCookiesAsync`) is a DPAPI-protected secondary fallback restore path; legacy plaintext payloads are read once and rewritten protected on the next save
285	- Bar role: `meter` (was `progressbar`) + language-independent parsing (v54.0): Claude.ai's usage page switched the bars from `[role=progressbar]` to `[role=meter]` (inside `data-cds=Meter`) and localizes all labels ("Sessão atual"/"Todos os modelos"/"Fable"). The scraper had queried `[role=progressbar][aria-valuenow]` everywhere, so it found zero bars → `extract()` returned null (inline bars kept showing the stale cached snapshot) and page isolation found no target (full settings page with sidebar rendered instead of the trimmed block). Fixed by matching both roles via the `BAR_SEL`/`BAR_ROLE_SEL`/`isBarRole()` helpers (kept dual so a revert or cached page still parses) across `findSection`, `findIsolationTarget`, `clearStaleInlineWidths` (must skip meter descendants too, or it wipes the inline fill `width:63%`), the trim CSS, and `extract`. Row identification is now language-independent: labels read via `aria-labelledby`→`getElementById` (`readBarLabelAndReset`) with the `.text-primary` column as fallback, session/weekly matched by multi-language keyword regex but ultimately by document order (session = first bar; weekly = the aggregate "all models" bar, which always precedes per-model bars like Fable — so weekly falls back to "first row after session", never a per-model bar). `readUsedPercent` prefers `aria-valuetext` ("63% usado"/"63% used") so extra-usage percent survives localization and the >100% case. The old `div[tabindex=-1].outline-none` isolation target is gone from the page; the bar→`closest('section')`→`parentElement` (`div.pb-8`) fallback now supplies it. Pure JS fix — `UsageSnapshot` field names and the C# side are unchanged
286	- Spend-limit-only pages and stale snapshots (issue #182, v214.0): `extract()` used to return null unless it found *two* rows, and `postSnapshot()` silently drops a null — so a page with a single meter (usage-based Enterprise seats: one monthly spend bar, no session/weekly limits; also any account whose second meter disappears, e.g. an expired included-credit grant that the `r !== sessionRow` fallback had been using as "weekly") never posted again, and the bars showed the cached snapshot forever. The weekly row is now optional: the snapshot carries `NoWeeklyLimit` (negative on purpose, so snapshots cached by older versions deserialize to false and keep their weekly row) and `ApplyUsageSnapshot` collapses `InlineWeeklyStack`/bar/pct when it is set. Separately, `UpdateInlineUsageStaleNotice()` shows a "Not updated since …" line (`InlineUsageStaleNotice`) when `LastUsageTimestamp` is older than `UsageSnapshotStaleAfter` (30 min — a healthy background refresh lands one per minute); evaluated on startup restore, after each scrape, after each background tick and on tab visibility change. Suppressed while the usage tab is the foreground tab, because the page there only posts on change and the timestamp can legitimately age while the data is live.
287	- Fable gated on usage credits (v215.0): Fable needs usage credits, so `extract()` also reads the balance from the header of `#extra-usage-credits-section` (`[data-settings-group-header]` → last child, e.g. `R$0`) into `UsageSnapshot.UsageCreditsBalance` (verbatim). `UsageSnapshot.IsZeroCreditBalance` (pure, unit-tested) is true only when the text has a digit and every digit is zero; `IsFableModelOffered()` reads it from the cached `LastUsageJson`. Fail-open on purpose: no snapshot, no section, no amount, or a snapshot cached by an older version (field absent) all keep Fable offered. Consumers: the 🤖 model menu (`ModelContextMenu_Opened`), both native-chat composer model menus, and the Recommend AI Model dialog picker — each still shows Fable when it is the current pick so the selection has a row; the dialog maps an advisor answer of `fable` to Opus with a note (the advisor schema itself is unchanged).
288	- Returning to the usage view after a manual account switch (v158.0): `TryRedirectToUsage`'s post-auth landing whitelist (`/new`, `/chats`, `/chat/`, `/projects`, `/recents`) deliberately excluded the root path, because `/` doubles as the signed-out home page and redirecting it unconditionally loops `/settings/usage → / → /settings/usage`. claude.ai drops a fresh sign-in on `/` about as often as on `/new`, so Switch Account → native "Log out" → sign in as a different user left the panel parked on the home page until the user pressed Refresh. `_sawSignedOutPage` (set whenever the embedded page visits `/login`, `/logout`, `/magic-link` or `/auth`) now promotes `/` to a landing, and `RedirectToUsageIfSettledAsync` requires a non-empty claude.ai `sessionKey` cookie (`HasClaudeSessionCookieAsync`) before navigating — a genuinely signed-out root reads no cookie and is left alone. The flag is cleared as the redirect fires, so a navigate that bounces straight back to `/` cannot re-arm it: one attempt per sign-out. The settle path re-checks `core.Source` both before and after the awaited cookie read, since the await gives the page another chance to move. `/onboarding` is deliberately *not* a landing — an account claude.ai forces through onboarding would ping-pong `/onboarding → /settings/usage` every ~6.5 s (1.5 s settle + 5 s debounce).
289	- Trim restore after Switch Account (`TryRestoreTrim`, v158.0): `SwitchAccountButton_Click` sets `window.__claudeSuppressTrim` so claude.ai's own chrome — and with it the account menu — stays visible. That flag lives on the document, so a full page load clears it by itself, but an SPA route change back to `/settings/usage` does not, leaving the raw settings page (sidebar and all) in the panel. Both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged` now clear the flag whenever the source is on `/settings/usage`, ahead of the redirect check.
290	- Following a Claude CLI account switch (v221.0): the bars come from the WebView2's own claude.ai session, which has nothing to do with the CLI's credentials, so `/logout` + `/login` typed into the terminal (or `claude auth login` anywhere) moved the agent to another account while the bars kept scraping, and refreshing, the old one. Only the ⚙ "Change Account" items signed the page out. `SyncUsageWithClaudeAccountAsync` runs on every background tick (ahead of the foreground-tab guard) and once before the startup refresh. It reads `oauthAccount` from the active side's `~/.claude.json` (the distro's copy for `ClaudeCodeWSL`, with the `wslpath` result cached per session). `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR` is honored on both sides (`GetClaudeJsonPath`, `${CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR:-$HOME}` under WSL), because the CLI then keeps the file in that folder and never writes the one in the home directory. It identifies the account as `accountUuid/organizationUuid`, so switching organizations under the same login counts as a switch too, since usage limits are per organization. It falls back to the e-mail address when the UUIDs are missing. No `oauthAccount` (between `/logout` and `/login`) or a half-written file reads as "unknown" and never as a switch. The account the page was last paired with is kept per side (`windows`/`wsl`) in `usage-account.json` next to the settings, not in the settings. Every VS window saves its whole in-memory settings on each scrape, so a second window would write the old account back and then sign the shared page out a second time. The first check on a side only records the account. A window can find the pairing already moved to the account it now reads, because another window handled the switch. It then only drops its own cached snapshot (`_usageAccountSeen`), since its bars would otherwise sit on the old numbers until the next successful scrape. A change calls `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync(pairedAccount)`, which clears the cached snapshot, signs the page out and shows a main-window info bar (`InfoBarSlot.UsageAccount`) with an "Open Claude Usage" link. It deliberately does not pop the tab, which could steal focus while the user types. The Change Account menu items pass no account, which forgets the pairing, so the CLI login that follows is adopted silently instead of being handled as a second switch.
291	  - `SignOutAsync` used to delete cookies only on a live instance. When none was alive (never built this session, torn down with its hidden tab by #131, or a timed-out build), only `shared_cookies.json` went away. The `sessionKey` stayed in the persistent profile, and the next rebuild came straight back as the old account. It now builds an instance first (`_clearProfileOnNextBuild` makes `InitializeWebViewAsync` clear the profile before `LoadSharedCookiesAsync` and the first navigation). It clears with `Profile.ClearBrowsingDataAsync(AllSite)` rather than claude.ai cookies alone, because a "Continue with Google" sign-in keeps its own session in the profile and would silently sign the old account back in. It then navigates to the usage URL, and it resets the cookie-save throttle so the new account's first scrape writes `shared_cookies.json` immediately. `SignOutUsageWindowIfActiveAsync` gets the control through `GetUsageControlAsync`, which creates the hidden tool window when this session has not yet done so.
292	- Corporate proxy interstitial handling (`TryHandleUrlBlock`): Detects when `core.Source` ends with `/urlblock.php` (iboss/Forcepoint/Zscaler style block pages) and injects a JS poller that retries up to 25× at 200ms looking for the Continue submit button — multiple selector fallbacks (`input[type=submit][name=ok]` → generic `input[type=submit]` → `button[type=submit]` → `button[name=ok]` → `form.submit()`). Works while the tool window is hidden because CoreWebView2 processes navigation and JS without a visible rendering surface. Throttled to one click per 3 s. Triggered from both `OnNavigationCompleted` and `OnSourceChanged`
293	- Scrollbox preservation (v73.0): `isolatePath()` used to mark *every* ancestor between the isolation target and `<body>` as `data-claude-usage-path`, whose CSS forces `display:block; height:auto; overflow:visible` — this silently deleted claude.ai's own internal scroll pane (a `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto` wrapper around the settings content), so anything below the initial fold (e.g. the Usage Credits spend/balance/buy-credits rows) was unreachable with no scrollbar at all. Fix: while walking up, the first ancestor whose *native* computed `overflow-y` is `auto`/`scroll` (checked before any of our own attributes could affect it) is tagged `data-claude-usage-scrollbox` instead of `-path`; every further ancestor above it is tagged the same way (`pastScrollbox` flag) since they're all part of its flex height-bounding chain. The `scrollbox` CSS rule only strips width caps/grid columns — it never touches `display`/`height`/`overflow`, so the pane's native scrollbar keeps working exactly as it does in a real browser tab.
294	  - Follow-up — the `keep` rule was the same bug (v73.0): the ancestor-side fix alone didn't restore scrolling, because `findIsolationTarget()` can resolve to a `tabindex=-1` dialog shell (not just the small `div.pb-8` block) when the page has one — that shell itself commonly uses `display:flex; flex-direction:column` to stack a header above the internally-scrolling body. The `[data-claude-usage-keep="1"]` rule was still forcing `display:block !important` on the target, which collapses that flex-column and strips the scrollable child's bounded height (its `flex-1`/`min-h-0` become no-ops once the parent isn't a flex container) — the shell's own untouched `overflow:hidden` then just clips the excess with no scrollbar, no matter what the ancestor-side fix does. `keep` now only widens the target (`width`/`max-width`/`margin`/`box-sizing`) and leaves `display`/`height`/`overflow`/`padding` completely alone, same principle as the `scrollbox` rule.
295	- Docked tab painting over its neighbour (v230.0): the WebView2 is a native child window, so WPF clipping and z-order never apply to it. Measured on a tab docked in the document well with the Output pane below: the control's bottom edge landed at the bottom of the Output pane, i.e. it was laid out ~280 px taller than the area the shell shows, so the shell clipped the WPF elements (status bar) while the native window kept painting over Output. `ClaudeUsageControl`'s guard (`#region WebView2 bounds guard`) runs 150 ms after `SizeChanged`/`IsVisibleChanged`/the frame's `OnSize`, and on a 2 s heartbeat while the control is loaded. (1) `ClampWebViewToVisibleArea` hit-tests the `WebArea` grid (it has a `Transparent` background on purpose — WPF hit testing skips an element with no brush) down its middle: WPF hit testing honors the shell's clip, so the first point that no longer hits one of this control's own visuals is where the pane ends (one hit test when nothing is cut off, a ~7-step binary search otherwise). The web view host then gets an explicit `Height` of the visible part with `VerticalAlignment=Top` (not `MaxHeight`: a non-stretched host sizes to its content and an `HwndHost` desires 0); the clamp is released when the area is fully visible again. (2) `RepairWebViewBounds` compares `GetWindowRect(WebView.Handle)` with where WPF put the element (`PointToScreen` + `ActualWidth/Height` × the DPI transform) through the pure `HostedWindowBounds.IsMisaligned` (2 px tolerance, an element with no area never counts); a mismatch must be seen on two consecutive checks before anything is done, then `NudgeWebViewLayout` (width −1 px and back), and if the window is still wrong `SnapWindowTo` (`SetWindowPos`). Three failed repairs in a row back it off for 60 s. The off-screen scraper is skipped. Diagnostics: every change of state is appended to `%LocalAppData%\ClaudeCodeExtension\usage-layout.log` (control/area size, visible height, the frame's own `GetFramePos`, and — only while clipped — the ancestor chain with each element's vertical extent and clip flags; restarted past 200 KB). If the overlap ever returns, that file says whether WPF's layout, the shell's clip or the window itself is the one that is off.
296	
297	- Native-mode composer usage button (v235.0, `Controls/ClaudeCodeControl.ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatUsageIndicator.cs`, `UI/ChatTranscriptView.xaml` `ComposerUsageButton`/`UsagePopup`): a ring after the composer's Permissions selector, shown only for Claude providers. The popup has two halves: the context window of the chat's last completed turn (`ClaudeStatusLineInput` captured in `CompleteNativeTurn`/`CompleteNativeTurnForSession` into `_mainStatusLine` or `NativeChatSessionState.LastStatusLine`, cleared by Clear Chat), and the plan limits read from the cached `LastUsageJson` (the same numbers as the inline bars, so `NoWeeklyLimit`/`HasExtraUsage` are honored). The ring fills with context %, or with the session limit before any turn has reported a window. `HandleScrapedSnapshot` calls `RefreshChatUsageIndicators()`, so an open popup updates in place. Opening the popup raises `UsageRequested`, handled by `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync`: the same account-switch guard the background timer uses first, then `Reload()` when the tab is visible, otherwise `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:false, updateWindowState:false, activate:false)`, so the tab never appears from a ring click. "See detailed breakdown" (`UsageDetailsRequested`) calls `EnsureUsageToolWindowAsync(showWindow:true)`, the same as the inline bars. The popup's "Updated / Not updated since" line uses `IsUsageSnapshotStale`. Formatting and ring geometry are pure (`ChatUsageIndicator`, unit-tested in `Tests/ChatUsageIndicatorTests.cs`). Popup rows (v236.0): label column `Auto`, value column `*` right-aligned with `CharacterEllipsis`; the border is `MinWidth=280`/`MaxWidth=440` instead of a fixed 280, because a long value ("0% used · Starts with your first message") in the old `*`/`Auto` layout squeezed the label column and drew over "Current session". `UsageNoPlanText` keeps `MaxWidth=256` so its wrapping does not stretch the popup. "Refreshing…" (v236.0): a ring click sets the view's `_usageRefreshing`, so the last line reads "Refreshing…" (snapshot pushes in the meantime only update the stored `_usageUpdatedText`) until the control calls `EndUsageRefresh()` on the clicked transcript when `RefreshUsageForIndicatorAsync` finishes. That task waits for real data: the off-screen path through `RefreshUsageInBackgroundAsync`'s own wait, the visible-tab `Reload()` path on `_indicatorScrapeTcs` (completed in `HandleScrapedSnapshot`, 15 s cap). A click while one is running joins the running `_indicatorRefresh` instead of starting another. Not F5-verified. The popup's wait is capped at `UsageRefreshTextCapMs` (20 s, v268.0): the off-screen path can chain a 10 s silent reload, a WebView2 rebuild (up to 30 s) and another 10 s wait, so "Refreshing…" could sit there over a minute after a fresh sign-in; the refresh itself keeps running and a later snapshot still updates the popup in place. Refresh ring (v276.0): the last line no longer swaps to "Refreshing…" (which hid the time); `UsageUpdatedRow` keeps the "Updated" text and shows `UsageRefreshSpinner` (10 px ring, tooltip "Refreshing…") beside it while `_usageRefreshing`. The rotation is started/stopped with `BeginAnimation` in `ShowUsageUpdatedText` only when the state flips, never by a style trigger (the v265.0 crash).
298	- Icon-font glyphs in reset text (v268.0): claude.ai renders some icons as Private Use Area characters, and on some rows (seen on the Italian weekly row) the only `.text-secondary` element of the label column holds such an icon instead of a reset date, so `readLabelAndReset` took `U+E027` as `WeeklyReset` and VS drew it as a box. The scraper now strips `U+E000–U+F8FF` before choosing the reset text; `ChatUsageIndicator.StripIconGlyphs` does the same on the C# side (popup rows via `PlanRowText`, inline reset labels) so snapshots cached before the fix render clean too.

Corrigi os três problemas na versão 300.0. O build Debug passa e os 1083 testes também. **Ainda não testei dentro do Visual Studio (F5)**, então a troca de conta ainda precisa ser testada lá.

**Por que ficava recarregando:** o claude.ai mudou a página de uso: `/settings/usage` agora redireciona para `/new#settings/usage` e abre as configurações como uma janela por cima do chat. A extensão não reconhecia esse endereço como a página de uso. Ela achava que era a tela de depois do login e voltava para a página de uso a cada ~6,5 s, e isso não parava.

**O que mudou:**
- **Sem recarga em loop:** a extensão agora reconhece os dois endereços da página de uso. Em `/new` ela não recorta nem lê nada.
- **Trocar de conta:** o menu de conta fica no chat, atrás da janela de configurações, por isso não dava para chegar nele. Agora o botão abre `/new`, abre o menu de conta e espera você trocar de conta ou entrar de novo. Depois volta sozinho para a tela de uso. Nesse tempo a atualização automática não tira você do menu. Se nada acontecer em 10 minutos, ele volta para a tela de uso.
- **Tela até o final:** a janela de uso ocupa a aba inteira, sem a faixa vazia embaixo e sem a coluna estreita. A rolagem chega até o fim. O X do claude.ai foi escondido, porque fechar a janela deixaria só o chat aberto.
- **E-mail no popup:** a última linha do popup de uso do chat mostra "Conta: seu@email". Funciona nos 20 idiomas.

Testei o script novo na página real do claude.ai com os seus cookies, no Edge, no tamanho do seu painel. A tela de uso ocupou a área inteira e trouxe os números e o e-mail. Em `/new` ele não mexeu em nada. Depois apaguei a cópia temporária dos cookies e os scripts do teste.
